expected.whyWePickedIt: A genuinely original, hands-on puzzle sandbox.

set.whyWePickedIt: That moment when a strange arrangement of blocks finally does what you hoped is the reason to try NodeCore. We'd choose it for friends who enjoy swapping theories, trying something ridiculous and eventually figuring out why it worked. The machinery gives that curiosity somewhere to go long after the first discoveries.

faq.a: Crafting happens in the world. Arrange materials and work on them directly. Give yourself time to experiment, because learning those interactions is a large part of the game.

faq.q: Will the game help me get started?
faq.a: There is a built-in guide and discovery system. Expect small nudges with few spoilers. We'd start there before looking up solutions and giving away the discoveries.
NodeCore supports multiplayer as well as solo play. Choose a server running NodeCore so everybody is working with the same game.

expected.whyWePickedIt: A hardcore survival experience on a free engine.

set.whyWePickedIt: A bed, a roof and drinking water make a surprisingly satisfying set of goals. Exile gives those ordinary things weight, then asks whether your camp can cope with the next season. We'd pick it for friends who enjoy planning a practical little settlement and earning every improvement to it.

faq.a: Find a campsite and get a bed under shelter before exhaustion catches up with you. Warmth, rest and drinking water deserve your attention before an ambitious building project.

faq.q: Which world generator should I choose?
faq.a: Start with Valleys, the project's standard choice. Carpathian is supported too, but the developers describe it as a harder, slower option.

faq.q: Why does my character struggle in bad weather?
faq.a: Exhaustion and temperature affect survival. Rest somewhere sheltered at a suitable temperature, and prepare clothing and supplies for the changing seasons.

expected.whyWePickedIt: A calm, handcrafted world to explore.

set.whyWePickedIt: We'd hand Asuna to the friend who stops every five minutes to scout a better place for the house. Its landscape variety gives wandering a purpose. The optional content packs also let your group decide how much survival to add, so you can spend an evening exploring without turning dinner into another deadline.

faq.q: Can I make the survival rules more relaxed?
faq.a: Yes. Asuna's content packs can be configured individually under Settings > Content: Games > Asuna. We'd look through those options before starting a shared world.

faq.q: Will I starve if I forget to eat?
faq.a: Starvation is disabled by default. Food grants benefits such as movement speed and health recovery, which diminish as you become hungry. You can enable starvation in the settings.
It lets you earn item duplication by discovering or creating the required items. That gives builders something to work toward while making large projects easier to supply.
